title: Finding Both Intercepts: Let the Axes Tell You What Becomes Zero

scenes.title: Where does 4x + 3y = 24 hit both axes?
body: We need the x-intercept and y-intercept.
The graph gives the rule: each axis forces one coordinate to zero.
scenes.narration: Find both intercepts of four x plus three y equals twenty-four. Here’s the idea: an intercept is simply where the line reaches an axis. So instead of memorizing two separate tricks, use what each axis means geometrically. One coordinate must be zero at every point on that axis.

scenes.title: The common mix-up
body: Do not set x = 0 just because you want the x-intercept.
scenes.substitution: Axis condition comes from the coordinate that disappears
scenes.narration: This is where students often mix things up. For the x-intercept, you set y equal to zero, not x. Why? Every point on the x-axis has height zero, so its y-coordinate is zero. Likewise, every point on the y-axis has x-coordinate zero. The axis itself tells you which variable disappears.

scenes.title: Find the x-intercept
scenes.narration: Start with the x-axis condition, y equals zero. Substituting gives four x plus three times zero equals twenty-four. The y-term vanishes, leaving four x equals twenty-four, so x equals six. That gives the point six comma zero. Notice why the algebra became simple: restricting the line to an axis removes one variable completely.

scenes.title: Find the y-intercept
scenes.narration: Now impose the y-axis condition, x equals zero. Four times zero disappears, so three y equals twenty-four and y equals eight. The y-intercept is zero comma eight. We are not using a different formula; we are asking where the same line satisfies a different axis condition.

scenes.title: Check the geometry and the equation
scenes.narration: Quick check: six comma zero gives twenty-four, and zero comma eight also gives twenty-four, so both points lie on the original line. The key idea is not which letter matches the intercept name. The key is which coordinate must be zero on that axis. The full lesson is available on SUMMIT. Find the complete lesson below.
